title: Maize Lethal Necrosis Disease on Maize

Header: Maize Lethal Necrosis Disease on Maize
Sugar cane mosaic virus and Maize chlorotic mottle virus Ukimwi wa Mahindi-Kiswahili, Miguna miguna-Luo, Koroito-Kalenjin

Prevention: Practice strict crop rotation for at least 2 seasons with non-cereal crops like beans, garlic, onions and vegetables
Plant maize only during the long season.
Avoid continuous planting of maize crop to stop the persistence of virus and possible vectors.
Avoid moving plants from infected regions to non-infected regions to reduce spread of disease
Plant early with fertilizer and manure to enhance crop nutrition and vigour
Keep the field free from weeds which may be alternate hosts to the vectors
Monitoring: Inspect the field every 3 to 4 days for: - Chlorotic mottle starting from the base of young leaves. - Necrosis of leaf margins progressing to the mid rib leading to drying of the whole leaf - Dwarfing and premature aging of plants

Inspect the field for vectors: - Use yellow sticky traps for beetles and grasshoppers - Use blue sticky to trap thrips - Examine plants early in the mornings before 11.00 am and after 3.00 pm as thrips tend to hide underneath the leaves in high temperatures
Act immediately when symptoms are noticed on one plant
Direct Control: Spray then uproot and destroy plants with typical symptoms. (see direct control yellow)
Farmers can use the maize stalk to make the silage but should destroy all infected cobs by burning or burying 1m deep to avoid mycotoxin contamination.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide always wear protective clothing.
Follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB)
Imidacloprid 6-10ml/20L to control maize thrips and leaf hoppers (vectors) e.g
Action: neonicoteinoid; IRAC code 4A WHO II (moderately hazardous)
Lambda-cyhalothrin 65ml/20L water to control maize thrips and leaf hoppers (vectors) e.g
Action: pyrethroid, quick active contact and stomach action; IRAC code 3
WHO II (moderately hazardous); Flammable; Apply twice in a planting season
